p.title: Interval ↔ set-builder

U = {0, 1, 2, …, 8}, A = {1, 3, 5}, B = {2, 4, 6}, C = {0, 2, 4, 6, 8}. Notice B sits wholly inside C (B ⊂ C). Shade A, then C, then the part of U outside both A and C.
A = {1, 2, 3, 4}, B = {3, 4, 5, 6}, C = {4, 6, 8}. Shade A ∪ B, B ∪ C, then A ∩ (B ∪ C) and (A ∩ B) ∪ (A ∩ C) — the same region: the distributive law!
A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, B = {2, 4, 6, 8}. Shade A − B, then B − A, then A ∩ B. The three disjoint pieces together make A ∪ B — shade that last.
U = {1, 2, …, 9}, A = {1, 2, 3, 4}, B = {2, 4, 6, 8}. Shade (A ∪ B)′ and then A′ ∩ B′, then (A ∩ B)′ and A′ ∪ B′. Same regions each time — De Morgan's laws.
A = {1, 2, 3}, B = {3, 4}. Plot every ordered pair (a, b) of A × B (first element across, second up). How many are there? n(A × B) = 3 × 2.

items.text: A prime number that is even

p.challenge: A die is thrown: A = “prime” = {2, 3, 5}, B = “odd” = {1, 3, 5}. Shade “A or B”, “A and B”, “A but not B” and “neither A nor B”.
S = {ω₁, ω₂, ω₃, ω₄} with P = 0.1, 0.3, 0.4, 0.2 — each between 0 and 1 and adding to 1, so the assignment is valid. P(E) = sum of P(ωᵢ) in E. Predict P({ω₂, ω₃}), then spin.
P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.3, P(A ∩ B) = 0.1 — shown as 10 equally likely outcomes. Shade A ∪ B (P = 0.5 + 0.3 − 0.1), then “neither A nor B”, then “A but not B”. Divide each count by 10.
